feedback.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $A$ to $C$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{AC}=\overset{\to }{AF}+\overset{\to }{FE}+\overset{\to }{EG}+\overset{\to }{GC}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/e24ac0b6cf4f039cd1e8b2e1aa5dd921ea637fb2fe46666a0091372dfce87d44.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{AF}=c,\,\overset{\to }{FE}=-a,\,\overset{\to }{EG}=-b\,\overset{\to }{GC}=d.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040990/assets/37c3758dc7a4c8a5b79c3e687e77f62090282410e3bf45bfade3494cd3b8055b.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AC} & =\overset{\to }{AF}+\overset{\to }{FE}+\overset{\to }{EG}+\overset{\to }{GC} \\  & =c+(-a)+(-b)+d \\  & =c-a-b+d.\end{aligned}
$$
